messages:
jess: Hey team — customer ACME reported p95/p99 latency regressions starting ~09:10 UTC, volume spike at 09:08. They see lots of 202/timeout-ish responses and long tail. Request IDs: req=acme-9a3f, acme-9a41. Similar to earlier queueing issues but not identical.

emily: Fwded from CS: customer says end-users hit app timeouts, blaming our API. They can repro with a single script hitting /v1/generate with burst concurrency 50 for 60s.

jess: Repro steps from customer: 
```
for i in $(seq 1 50); do curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"model":"rwd-4b","input":"hello"}' &
done
wait
```
They get many long waits and 504s, p99 ~18s.

aj: I'm on it. Initial look at ingress shows a sudden concentrated spike from ACME's IPs at 09:07-09:12. Admission control started rejecting but backlog grew. Snapshot of admission metrics: queued_requests=162, inflight_workers=48, worker_queue_len_per_shard=[34,28,50,50].

mike: Thanks @aj. Could be hot-partitioning of tenant routing. I see the tenant weight for ACME is 0.9 so most work pinned to a small worker set. That plus auth token reuse might be causing KV/cache thrash. Looking at runtime logs for req acme-9a3f: 
```
[09:09:12] request=req=acme-9a3f tenant=acme shard=3 admitted
[09:09:12] enqueue -> worker=shard-3 queue_pos=45
[09:09:30] worker-oom? evicting kv-cache segment
[09:09:35] request=req=acme-9a3f started tokenization
[09:09:50] request=req=acme-9a3f generate step k=23 ms=12000
```
Looks like long stall inside generate.

jess: Customer said they didn't change client behavior, only traffic ramped. Are there any ongoing deploys?

deploy-bot: deploy rwd-runtime v3.12.1 to canary started at 09:05 UTC by mike.

aj: That aligns. Canary nodes had a config change to concurrency-split heuristic (sticky-sharding enabled). Might be causing uneven routing. Rolling back that canary to mitigate.

mike: I'm preparing a rollback of the heuristic flag on canary. Temp mitigation we can apply: reduce tenant affinity for ACME, enable fair-queueing on the affected shard, and bump admission_concurrency from 64->80 across the group to relieve queued backpressure while we validate rollback.

jess: Can we do quick A/B so customer impact is measured? ACME willing to route 5% traffic to fallback model or lower tokens.

aj: I'll do a hotpatch: set tenant_affinity.scale=0.2 for tenant=acme on canary and enable fast-fail for queue_pos>100. Triggering now.

mike: Rollback applied to canary at 09:23 UTC (reverted sticky-sharding), and I pushed fair-queueing flag to affected workers.

aj: Observability after mitigations: queued_requests dropped 162 -> 18 in 3m, p99 dropped 18s -> 420ms for canary subset. Customer is reporting improvement when routing 5% traffic to fallback.

tina: I'll open an incident playbook entry and follow-up tasks:
- root-cause: canary sticky-sharding heuristic created hot shard for tenant with high affinity -> worker queue saturation + KV cache thrash
- short-term: rollback canary, tenant_affinity throttle, fair-queueing, fast-fail >100
- long-term: tune tenant-weight caps, add autoscale for shard hotness, add synthetic periodic churn tests for affinity changes

mike: PR for rollback: https://git.internal/r/redwood/runtime/pulls/542 (revert sticky-sharding), change-id: rrt-542.

jess: Customer confirmed lower latencies after we routed fallback model. They're running extended test. I'll keep them updated.

emily: CS asked for a short explanation phrased for customer: 'We identified a recent runtime change that concentrated ACME's requests onto fewer workers. That created a local queue and cache churn, causing long tail latency. We rolled back the change and applied fair-queueing and throttles; you should see normal latency now.'

tina: Follow-ups assigned: mike (runtime config audit), aj (hotpatch playbook), support (jess) to close with customer when stable, eng-sre (tina) to track long-term items.

jess: Marking this thread as ongoing. I'll post final closure once ACME completes their 30m verification. :white_check_mark:
